data.one_liner: A lightweight convention-based syntax highlighting widget for text code.
data.what_it_does: It provides a syntax highlighting widget that parses input code using convention-based rules such as capitalized identifiers for classes and comments. It also supports custom themes, line numbers, selectable text, and Google Fonts integration.
use_when: You want a simple syntax highlighter without complex configuration.
You want to display code snippets with automatic convention-based highlighting.
You need optional features like line numbers, copy buttons, and Google Fonts styling.
avoid_when: You need deep AST-based parsing for full language compilation accuracy.
You require advanced language grammars that go beyond basic convention rules.
strengths: Easy to set up and use as a standard Flutter widget.
Supports Google Fonts integration out of the box.
Includes default themes and custom theme support.
weaknesses: Relies on convention-based regex parsing rather than strict language parsers.
Limited built-in configuration for custom grammars beyond default conventions.
